cases.sentence: В эту минуту дверь тихо отворилась, и в комнату, робко озираясь, вошла одна ___.
cases.explain: Девушка is the grammatical subject of вошла (entered), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Всё стоит ___ пять-шесть, но мне дорого, память.
cases.explain: An approximate quantity expression (рублей пять-шесть) requires the genitive plural of the counted noun.

cases.sentence: Ведь он теперь это дело… ну, вот, по этому ___… вот вчера-то вы говорили… ведет?
cases.explain: The preposition по (concerning, regarding) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Сначала Раскольников указал было ей ___ в углу дивана, где сидел Зосимов.
cases.explain: Место is the direct object of указал (pointed out), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Но Авдотья Романовна это заметила. Она пристально и с беспокойством следила за ___.
cases.explain: The preposition за (after, following with the eyes) governs the instrumental case with следить.

cases.sentence: Раскольников указал было ей место в ___ дивана, где сидел Зосимов.
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating location governs the prepositional case, and угол takes the special locative ending -у.

cases.sentence: Это был ___ лет пятидесяти, росту повыше среднего, дородный, с широкими и крутыми плечами.
cases.explain: Человек functions as the nominative predicate noun after был (was).

reading.ru: В эту минуту дверь тихо отворилась, и в комнату, робко озираясь, вошла одна девушка.
reading.question: Who quietly entered the room in the middle of the family conversation?
options: A young woman glancing around timidly
reading.correct: A young woman glancing around timidly
reading.explain: The door quietly opened and a young woman, looking around timidly, entered the room.

reading.ru: Это была Софья Семеновна Мармеладова.
reading.question: Who turned out to be the young woman who entered?
reading.correct: Sofya Semyonovna Marmeladova (Sonya)
reading.explain: The text identifies her directly as Sofya Semyonovna Marmeladova.

reading.ru: Ах… это вы?.. — сказал Раскольников в чрезвычайном удивлении и вдруг сам смутился.
reading.question: How did Raskolnikov react upon recognizing Sonya?
options: With extreme surprise, and he became embarrassed himself
By pretending not to know her
reading.correct: With extreme surprise, and he became embarrassed himself
reading.explain: He said, 'Ah... it's you?..' in extreme surprise, and suddenly became embarrassed himself.

reading.ru: Я вас совсем не ожидал, — заторопился он, останавливая ее взглядом.
reading.question: What did Raskolnikov say to Sonya as she seemed about to flee in embarrassment?
options: That he hadn't expected her at all, while stopping her with a look
That he was too tired to speak with her
reading.correct: That he hadn't expected her at all, while stopping her with a look
reading.explain: He hurriedly said he hadn't expected her at all, holding her back with his gaze.

reading.ru: — Я…  я…  зашла на одну минуту, простите, что вас обеспокоила, — заговорила она, запинаясь.
reading.question: How did Sonya explain her visit, stammering with embarrassment?
options: That she came for just one minute and apologized for disturbing them
That she came to demand money
That she came to warn him about the police
That she came uninvited to see Dunya
reading.correct: That she came for just one minute and apologized for disturbing them
reading.explain: Stammering, Sonya says she came for just a minute and apologizes for disturbing them.

reading.ru: — Маменька, — сказал он твердо и настойчиво, — это Софья Семеновна Мармеладова, дочь того самого несчастного господина Мармеладова, которого вчера в моих глазах раздавили лошади и о котором я уже вам говорил…
reading.question: How did Raskolnikov introduce Sonya to his mother?
options: As the daughter of the unfortunate Marmeladov who was run over by horses
As a family friend from his university days
reading.correct: As the daughter of the unfortunate Marmeladov who was run over by horses
reading.explain: He firmly introduces her as Sofya Semyonovna, daughter of the unfortunate Marmeladov, killed by horses before his eyes.

reading.ru: Нет-с, всё прошло… Ведь уж слишком видно, отчего смерть была; не беспокоили; только вот жильцы сердятся.
reading.question: What did Sonya say about any trouble from the police regarding her father's death?
options: There was no trouble, but the tenants were annoyed (about the body)
The police had arrested Katerina Ivanovna
The landlady had thrown them out
reading.correct: There was no trouble, but the tenants were annoyed (about the body)
reading.explain: Sonya explains that everything passed without trouble from the police, but the tenants are annoyed.

reading.ru: Это было худенькое, совсем худенькое и бледное личико, довольно неправильное, какое-то востренькое, с востреньким маленьким носом и подбородком.
reading.question: How is Sonya's face described as Raskolnikov studies her?
options: Thin, pale, and somewhat irregular with a pointed look
reading.correct: Thin, pale, and somewhat irregular with a pointed look
reading.explain: Her face is described as thin, quite thin and pale, rather irregular, somewhat sharp-featured.

reading.ru: — Вы нам всё вчера отдали! — проговорила вдруг в ответ Сонечка, каким-то сильным и скорым шепотом, вдруг опять сильно потупившись.
reading.question: What did Sonya suddenly blurt out in response to Raskolnikov's remark about his poor room?
options: That he had given them everything yesterday
That her father would have been proud
That the room reminded her of her own
reading.correct: That he had given them everything yesterday
reading.explain: Sonechka suddenly said, in a strong, quick whisper, that he had given them everything yesterday.

reading.ru: Родя, — сказала она, вставая, — мы, разумеется, вместе обедаем.
reading.question: What did Pulkheria Alexandrovna announce as she prepared to leave with Dunya?
options: That they would, of course, dine together later
That they were leaving for the train station
That she would not return that day
That Luzhin was joining them for dinner
reading.correct: That they would, of course, dine together later
reading.explain: Rising, she says, 'Rodya, we shall, of course, dine together.'

reading.ru: Ну вот и славно! — сказал он Соне, возвращаясь к себе и ясно посмотрев на нее, — упокой господь мертвых, а живым еще жить!
reading.question: What did Raskolnikov say to Sonya after his mother and sister left?
options: That the dead should rest, but the living must still live
That she should also leave immediately
That he no longer wanted to talk about her father
That she should thank his mother
reading.correct: That the dead should rest, but the living must still live
reading.explain: He says brightly to Sonya, 'God rest the dead, but the living must still live!'

reading.ru: Опять говорю вам, маменька, он еще очень болен. Неужели вы не видите?
reading.question: How did Dunya explain her brother's strange behavior to their mother?
options: That he was still very ill
That he was simply rude by nature
That Luzhin had poisoned his mind against them
reading.correct: That he was still very ill
reading.explain: Dunya repeats to her mother that he is still very ill, asking if she doesn't see it.

reading.ru: Предчувствие у меня такое, Дуня.
reading.question: What did Pulkheria Alexandrovna admit having about Sonya?
options: A premonition/feeling that Sonya was somehow central to things
A dislike based on her appearance
A memory of meeting her before
A hope that she would help Raskolnikov
reading.correct: A premonition/feeling that Sonya was somehow central to things
reading.explain: She tells Dunya she has a premonition (that Sonya is somehow at the heart of the matter).

reading.ru: А Петр Петрович негодный сплетник, — вдруг отрезала Дунечка.
reading.question: What sharp remark did Dunya make about Luzhin?
options: That he was a worthless gossip
That he was the kindest man she knew
That he was too busy to notice anything
reading.correct: That he was a worthless gossip
reading.explain: Dunechka suddenly cut in sharply, calling Pyotr Petrovich a worthless gossip.

reading.ru: Ты ведь знаешь этого… Как его!.. Порфирия Петровича?
reading.question: Whom did Raskolnikov ask Razumikhin about regarding the pawned items?
reading.correct: Porfiry Petrovich
reading.explain: Raskolnikov asks Razumikhin if he knows Porfiry Petrovich, who is handling the murder investigation.

reading.ru: Всё стоит рублей пять-шесть, но мне дорого, память.
reading.question: How much were the pawned items (the ring and watch) worth to Raskolnikov?
options: Only about five or six roubles, but precious as keepsakes
reading.correct: Only about five or six roubles, but precious as keepsakes
reading.explain: He says it's all worth about five or six roubles, but it's precious to him as a memento.

reading.ru: Отнюдь не в часть и непременно к Порфирию! — крикнул в каком-то необыкновенном волнении Разумихин.
reading.question: What did Razumikhin insist Raskolnikov do about reclaiming his pawned items?
options: Go directly to Porfiry rather than to the police station
reading.correct: Go directly to Porfiry rather than to the police station
reading.explain: Razumikhin, strangely excited, insists it must by no means be the police station, but definitely Porfiry.

reading.ru: Соня дала свой адрес и при этом покраснела.
reading.question: What did Sonya do when Raskolnikov asked where she lived?
options: She gave her address and blushed
She wrote it down on paper
reading.correct: She gave her address and blushed
reading.explain: Sonya gave her address, blushing as she did so.

reading.ru: Он провожал ее с самого выхода из ворот.
reading.question: What was the mysterious stranger doing as Sonya walked home?
options: Following her since she left through the gate
Waiting for her at her apartment
reading.correct: Following her since she left through the gate
reading.explain: The stranger had been following her since she came out through the gate.

reading.ru: «Так куда же к себе? Видел где-то это лицо, — думал он, припоминая лицо Сони…
reading.question: What did the stranger think while trying to recall where he had seen Sonya's face?
options: That he had seen her face somewhere before
That she looked exactly like his late wife
That she resembled a wanted criminal
That she must be someone's servant
reading.correct: That he had seen her face somewhere before
reading.explain: He thinks to himself, wondering where she lives, that he has seen this face somewhere before.

reading.ru: Это был человек лет пятидесяти, росту повыше среднего, дородный, с широкими и крутыми плечами, что придавало ему несколько сутуловатый вид.
reading.question: How is the stranger following Sonya physically described?
options: A stout man of about fifty, above average height with broad shoulders
reading.correct: A stout man of about fifty, above average height with broad shoulders
reading.explain: He is described as a man of about fifty, taller than average, stout, with broad, hunched shoulders.

reading.ru: Вы у Капернаумова стоите! — сказал он, смотря на Соню и смеясь.
reading.question: What coincidence did the stranger point out to Sonya about their lodgings?
options: That she lived at Kapernaumov's, right next to his own lodging
That they had the same landlord
That she lived in his old apartment
That her neighbor was his cousin
reading.correct: That she lived at Kapernaumov's, right next to his own lodging
reading.explain: He tells her, laughing, that she lives at Kapernaumov's — right beside his own rooms.

reading.ru: Соседи, — продолжал он как-то особенно весело. — Я ведь всего третий день в городе.
reading.question: How long had the stranger claimed to be in the city?
reading.correct: Only the third day
reading.explain: He continues cheerfully, saying that he has been in the city only the third day.

reading.ru: Экой ведь наивный дурак!
reading.question: What did Raskolnikov silently think of Razumikhin's naive questions on the way to Porfiry's?
options: That he was such a naive fool
That he should be a detective himself
reading.correct: That he was such a naive fool
reading.explain: Raskolnikov thinks to himself, 'What a naive fool!' regarding Razumikhin's innocent questions.

reading.ru: Раскольников до того смеялся, что, казалось, уж и сдержать себя не мог, так со смехом и вступили в квартиру Порфирия Петровича.
reading.question: In what state did Raskolnikov and Razumikhin arrive at Porfiry Petrovich's apartment?
reading.correct: Laughing uncontrollably
reading.explain: Raskolnikov was laughing so hard he seemed unable to stop, and they entered Porfiry's apartment still laughing.

highlight.question: Which sentence explains why Raskolnikov did not immediately recognize Sofya?
sentences: Все обратились к ней с удивлением и любопытством.
Раскольников не узнал ее с первого взгляда.
Это была Софья Семеновна Мармеладова.
Вчера видел он ее в первый раз, но в такую минуту, при такой обстановке и в таком костюме, что в памяти его отразился образ совсем другого лица.
Теперь это была скромно и даже бедно одетая девушка, очень еще молоденькая, почти похожая на девочку, с скромною и приличною манерой, с ясным, но как будто несколько запуганным лицом.
highlight.explain: He had only seen her once before under very different circumstances and in different clothes, so her modest appearance now seemed unfamiliar to him.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows Raskolnikov's attempt to persuade Sofya to give him a few moments?
sentences: — Постараюсь непременно…  непременно, — отвечал Раскольников, привстав тоже и тоже запинаясь и не договаривая…
— Сделайте одолжение, садитесь, — сказал он вдруг, — мне надо с вами поговорить.
Пожалуйста, — вы, может быть, торопитесь, — сделайте одолжение, подарите мне две минуты…
highlight.explain: Raskolnikov politely appeals to her to spare him just two minutes of her time, assuming she might be in a hurry.

highlight.question: Which sentence reveals the mother's unexpected relief at leaving Raskolnikov's apartment?
sentences: — Господи, Дунечка!
— заговорила тотчас же Пульхерия Александровна, как вышли на улицу, — вот ведь теперь сама точно рада, что мы ушли: легче как-то.
Ну, думала ли я вчера, в вагоне, что даже этому буду радоваться!
highlight.explain: Pulkheria Alexandrovna expresses surprise to find comfort in leaving, noting that the atmosphere had been oppressive.

highlight.question: Which sentence demonstrates that Raskolnikov was not yet well acquainted with Sofya?
sentences: — Совсем ничего не сидит!
— с досадой вскрикнула Дуня.
— И какие вы с вашими предчувствиями, мамаша!
Он только со вчерашнего дня с ней знаком, а теперь, как вошла, не узнал.
highlight.explain: Dunya points out that he has only known Sofya since the previous day, so his failure to recognize her is not particularly meaningful.

highlight.question: Which sentence conveys enthusiasm about how circumstances have worked out favorably?
sentences: — А он очень, очень, очень, очень будет рад с тобой познакомиться!
Я много говорил ему о тебе, в разное время…
И вчера говорил.
Так ты знал старуху?
Ве-ли-ко-лепно это всё обернулось!..
Софья Ивановна…
highlight.explain: Someone exclaims with delight that everything has turned out magnificently, suggesting a fortunate convergence of events.

highlight.question: Which sentence captures Sofya's frightened and anguished emotional state?
sentences: — Только уж не сегодня, пожалуйста, не сегодня!
— бормотала она с замиранием сердца, точно кого-то упрашивая, как ребенок в испуге.
Ко мне…  в эту комнату…  он увидит…  о господи!
highlight.explain: The description shows her murmuring desperately with a sinking heart, begging like a frightened child, revealing her deep anxiety.
